# fd

`fd` is a program to find entries in your filesystem.
It is a simple, fast and user-friendly alternative to `find`.
While it does not aim to support all of `find`'s powerful functionality, it provides sensible
(opinionated) defaults for a majority of use cases.

## Features

* Intuitive syntax: `fd PATTERN` instead of `find -iname '*PATTERN*'`.
* Regular expression (default) and glob-based patterns.
* Very fast due to parallelized directory traversal.
* Uses colors to highlight different file types (same as `ls`).
* Supports parallel command execution
* Smart case: the search is case-insensitive by default. It switches to
  case-sensitive if the pattern contains an uppercase character.
* Ignores hidden directories and files, by default.
* Ignores patterns from your `.gitignore`, by default.
* The command name is *50%* shorter than `find` :-).

## Demo

![Demo](doc/screencast.svg)

## How to use

First, to get an overview of all available command line options, you can either run
`fd -h` for a concise help message or `fd --help` for a more detailed version.

### Simple search

*fd* is designed to find entries in your filesystem. The most basic search you can perform is to
run *fd* with a single argument: the search pattern. For example, assume that you want to find an
old script of yours (the name included `netflix`):
``` bash
> fd netfl
Software/python/imdb-ratings/netflix-details.py
```
If called with just a single argument like this, *fd* searches the current directory recursively
for any entries that *contain* the pattern `netfl`.

### Regular expression search

The search pattern is treated as a regular expression. Here, we search for entries that start
with `x` and end with `rc`:
``` bash
> cd /etc
> fd '^x.*rc$'
X11/xinit/xinitrc
X11/xinit/xserverrc
```

### Specifying the root directory

If we want to search a specific directory, it can be given as a second argument to *fd*:
``` bash
> fd passwd /etc
/etc/default/passwd
/etc/pam.d/passwd
/etc/passwd
```

### List all files, recursively

*fd* can be called with no arguments. This is very useful to get a quick overview of all entries
in the current directory, recursively (similar to `ls -R`):
``` bash
> cd fd/tests
> fd
testenv
testenv/mod.rs
tests.rs
```

If you want to use this functionality to list all files in a given directory, you have to use
a catch-all pattern such as `.` or `^`:
``` bash
> fd . fd/tests/
testenv
testenv/mod.rs
tests.rs
```

### Searching for a particular file extension

Often, we are interested in all files of a particular type. This can be done with the `-e` (or
`--extension`) option. Here, we search for all Markdown files in the fd repository:
``` bash
> cd fd
> fd -e md
CONTRIBUTING.md
README.md
```

The `-e` option can be used in combination with a search pattern:
``` bash
> fd -e rs mod
src/fshelper/mod.rs
src/lscolors/mod.rs
tests/testenv/mod.rs
```

### Searching for a particular file name

 To find files with exactly the provided search pattern, use the `-g` (or `--glob`) option:
``` bash
> fd -g libc.so /usr
/usr/lib32/libc.so
/usr/lib/libc.so
```

### Hidden and ignored files

By default, *fd* does not search hidden directories and does not show hidden files in the
search results. To disable this behavior, we can use the `-H` (or `--hidden`) option:
``` bash
> fd pre-commit
> fd -H pre-commit
.git/hooks/pre-commit.sample
```

If we work in a directory that is a Git repository (or includes Git repositories), *fd* does not
search folders (and does not show files) that match one of the `.gitignore` patterns. To disable
this behavior, we can use the `-I` (or `--no-ignore`) option:
``` bash
> fd num_cpu
> fd -I num_cpu
target/debug/deps/libnum_cpus-f5ce7ef99006aa05.rlib
```

To really search *all* files and directories, simply combine the hidden and ignore features to show
everything (`-HI`) or use `-u`/`--unrestricted`.

### Matching the full path

By default, *fd* only matches the filename of each file. However, using the `--full-path` or `-p` option,
you can match against the full path:

``` bash
> fd -p -g '**/.git/config'
```

### Command execution

Instead of just showing the search results, you can use the `-x`/`--exec` option for parallel command execution:

``` bash
> fd -e jpg -x convert {} {.}.png
```

This runs `convert input.jpg input.png` for each `.jpg` file found. The `{}` is a placeholder for the search result.
You can also use `{.}` to get the path without extension, `{/}` for the basename, and `{//}` for the parent directory.

For sequential command execution, use `-X`/`--exec-batch`:
``` bash
> fd -e rs -X wc -l
```

### Excluding specific files or directories

You can exclude specific files or directories with the `-E` (or `--exclude`) option:
``` bash
> fd -e py -E '__pycache__'
```

### Deleting files

You can use `fd` with `-X` to delete all files that match a pattern:
``` bash
> fd -H '^\.DS_Store$' -X rm
```
(Use with caution!)

### Command-line options

A full overview of all available command-line options can be viewed by running `fd --help`.

The most important options are:

- `-H`, `--hidden`: Search hidden files and directories
- `-I`, `--no-ignore`: Don't respect ignore files (`.gitignore`, `.ignore`, etc.)
- `-u`, `--unrestricted`: Alias for `--hidden --no-ignore`
- `-s`, `--case-sensitive`: Case-sensitive search (default: smart case)
- `-i`, `--ignore-case`: Case-insensitive search
- `-g`, `--glob`: Glob-based search (instead of regular expression)
- `-F`, `--fixed-strings`: Treat pattern as a literal string
- `-a`, `--absolute-path`: Show absolute paths
- `-l`, `--list-details`: Use a detailed listing format like `ls -l`
- `-L`, `--follow`: Follow symbolic links
- `-p`, `--full-path`: Match against the full path
- `-d`, `--max-depth <depth>`: Set maximum search depth
- `-t`, `--type <filetype>`: Filter by type: `f` (file), `d` (directory), `l` (symlink), etc.
- `-e`, `--extension <ext>`: Filter by file extension
- `-E`, `--exclude <pattern>`: Exclude files/directories matching the given glob pattern
- `-x`, `--exec <cmd>`: Execute command for each search result (parallel)
- `-X`, `--exec-batch <cmd>`: Execute command with all search results at once
- `-c`, `--color <when>`: When to use color: `never`, `auto`, `always`
- `-j`, `--threads <num>`: Set number of threads for searching & executing
- `--changed-within <date|duration>`: Filter by file modification time (newer than)
- `--changed-before <date|duration>`: Filter by file modification time (older than)
- `-o`, `--owner <user:group>`: Filter by owning user and/or group
- `-S`, `--size <size>`: Filter by file size
- `--base-directory <path>`: Change current working directory

## License

`fd` is distributed under the terms of both the MIT License and the Apache License 2.0.

See the LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT files for license details.

*fd* is designed to find entries in your filesystem. The most basic search you can perform is to
run *fd* with a single argument: the search pattern. For example, assume that you want to find an
old script of yours (the name included `netflix`):
``` bash
> fd netfl
Software/python/imdb-ratings/netflix-details.py
```
If called with just a single argument like this, *fd* searches the current directory recursively
for any entries that *contain* the pattern `netfl`.

### Regular expression search

The search pattern is treated as a regular expression. Here, we search for entries that start
with `x` and end with `rc`:
``` bash
> cd /etc
> fd '^x.*rc$'
X11/xinit/xinitrc
X11/xinit/xserverrc
```

### Specifying the root directory

If we want to search a specific directory, it can be given as a second argument to *fd*:
``` bash
> fd passwd /etc
/etc/default/passwd
/etc/pam.d/passwd
/etc/passwd
```

### List all files, recursively

*fd* can be called with no arguments. This is very useful to get a quick overview of all entries
in the current directory, recursively (similar to `ls -R`):
``` bash
> cd fd/tests
> fd
testenv
testenv/mod.rs
tests.rs
```

If you want to use this functionality to list all files in a given directory, you have to use
a catch-all pattern such as `.` or `^`:
``` bash
> fd . fd/tests/
testenv
testenv/mod.rs
tests.rs
```

### Searching for a particular file extension

Often, we are interested in all files of a particular type. This can be done with the `-e` (or
`--extension`) option. Here, we search for all Markdown files in the fd repository:
``` bash
> cd fd
> fd -e md
CONTRIBUTING.md
README.md
```

The `-e` option can be used in combination with a search pattern:
``` bash
> fd -e rs mod
src/fshelper/mod.rs
src/lscolors/mod.rs
tests/testenv/mod.rs
```

### Searching for a particular file name

 To find files with exactly the provided search pattern, use the `-g` (or `--glob`) option:
``` bash
> fd -g libc.so /usr
/usr/lib32/libc.so
/usr/lib/libc.so
```

### Hidden and ignored files

By default, *fd* does not search hidden directories and does not show hidden files in the
search results. To disable this behavior, we can use the `-H` (or `--hidden`) option:
``` bash
> fd pre-commit
> fd -H pre-commit
.git/hooks/pre-commit.sample
```

If we work in a directory that is a Git repository (or includes Git repositories), *fd* does not
search folders (and does not show files) that match one of the `.gitignore` patterns. To disable
this behavior, we can use the `-I` (or `--no-ignore`) option:
``` bash
> fd num_cpu
> fd -I num_cpu
target/debug/deps/libnum_cpus-f5ce7ef99006aa05.rlib
```

To really search *all* files and directories, simply combine the hidden and ignore features to show
everything (`-HI`) or use `-u`/`--unrestricted`.

### Matching the full path

By default, *fd* only matches the filename of each file. However, using the `--full-path` or `-p` option,
you can match against the full path:

``` bash
> fd -p -g '**/.git/config'
```

### Command execution

Instead of just showing the search results, you can use the `-x`/`--exec` option for parallel command execution:

``` bash
> fd -e jpg -x convert {} {.}.png
```

This runs `convert input.jpg input.png` for each `.jpg` file found. The `{}` is a placeholder for the search result.
You can also use `{.}` to get the path without extension, `{/}` for the basename, and `{//}` for the parent directory.

For sequential command execution, use `-X`/`--exec-batch`:
``` bash
> fd -e rs -X wc -l
```

### Excluding specific files or directories

You can exclude specific files or directories with the `-E` (or `--exclude`) option:
``` bash
> fd -e py -E '__pycache__'
```

### Deleting files

You can use `fd` with `-X` to delete all files that match a pattern:
``` bash
> fd -H '^\.DS_Store$' -X rm
```
(Use with caution!)

### Command-line options

A full overview of all available command-line options can be viewed by running `fd --help`.

The most important options are:

- `-H`, `--hidden`: Search hidden files and directories
- `-I`, `--no-ignore`: Don't respect ignore files (`.gitignore`, `.ignore`, etc.)
- `-u`, `--unrestricted`: Alias for `--hidden --no-ignore`
- `-s`, `--case-sensitive`: Case-sensitive search (default: smart case)
- `-i`, `--ignore-case`: Case-insensitive search
- `-g`, `--glob`: Glob-based search (instead of regular expression)
- `-F`, `--fixed-strings`: Treat pattern as a literal string
- `-a`, `--absolute-path`: Show absolute paths
- `-l`, `--list-details`: Use a detailed listing format like `ls -l`
- `-L`, `--follow`: Follow symbolic links
- `-p`, `--full-path`: Match against the full path
- `-d`, `--max-depth <depth>`: Set maximum search depth
- `-t`, `--type <filetype>`: Filter by type: `f` (file), `d` (directory), `l` (symlink), etc.
- `-e`, `--extension <ext>`: Filter by file extension
- `-E`, `--exclude <pattern>`: Exclude files/directories matching the given glob pattern
- `-x`, `--exec <cmd>`: Execute command for each search result (parallel)
- `-X`, `--exec-batch <cmd>`: Execute command with all search results at once
- `-c`, `--color <when>`: When to use color: `never`, `auto`, `always`
- `-j`, `--threads <num>`: Set number of threads for searching & executing
- `--changed-within <date|duration>`: Filter by file modification time (newer than)
- `--changed-before <date|duration>`: Filter by file modification time (older than)
- `-o`, `--owner <user:group>`: Filter by owning user and/or group
- `-S`, `--size <size>`: Filter by file size
- `--base-directory <path>`: Change current working directory

"             '-': file size must be less than or equal to this\n"
"          \n"
"          If neither '+' nor '-' is specified, file size must be exactly equal to this.\n"
"             'NUM':  The numeric size (e.g. 500)\n"
"             'UNIT': The units for NUM. They are not case-sensitive.\n"
"          Allowed unit values:\n"
"              'b':  bytes\n"
"              'k':  kilobytes (base ten, 10^3 = 1000 bytes)\n"
"              'm':  megabytes\n"
"              'g':  gigabytes\n"
"              't':  terabytes\n"
"              'ki': kibibytes (base two, 2^10 = 1024 bytes)\n"
"              'mi': mebibytes\n"
"              'gi': gibibytes\n"
"              'ti': tebibytes\n"
"\n"
"      --changed-within <date|dur>\n"
"          Filter results based on the file modification time. Files with modification times\n"
"          greater than the argument are returned. The argument can be provided as a specific point\n"
"          in time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or @timestamp) or as a duration (10h, 1d, 35min). If the\n"
"          time is not specified, it defaults to 00:00:00. '--change-newer-than', '--newer', or\n"
"          '--changed-after' can be used as aliases.\n"
"          \n"
"          Examples: \n"
"              --changed-within 2weeks \n"
"              --change-newer-than '2018-10-27 10:00:00' \n"
"              --newer 2018-10-27 \n"
"              --changed-after 1day\n"
"\n"
"      --changed-before <date|dur>\n"
"          Filter results based on the file modification time. Files with modification times less\n"
"          than the argument are returned. The argument can be provided as a specific point in time\n"
"          (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or @timestamp) or as a duration (10h, 1d, 35min).\n"
"          '--change-older-than' or '--older' can be used as aliases.\n"
"          \n"
"          Examples: \n"
"              --changed-before '2018-10-27 10:00:00' \n"
"              --change-older-than 2weeks \n"
"              --older 2018-10-27\n"
"\n"
"  -o, --owner <user:group>\n"
"          Filter files by their user and/or group. Format: [(user|uid)][:(group|gid)]. Either side\n"
"          is optional. Precede either side with a '!' to exclude files instead.\n"
"          \n"
"          Examples: \n"
"              --owner john \n"
"              --owner :students \n"
"              --owner '!john:students'\n"
"\n"
"      --format <fmt>\n"
"          Print results according to template\n"
"\n"
"  -x, --exec <cmd>...\n"
"          Execute a command for each search result in parallel (use --threads=1 for sequential\n"
"          command execution). There is no guarantee of the order commands are executed in, and the\n"
"          order should not be depended upon. All positional arguments following --exec are\n"
"          considered to be arguments to the command - not to fd. It is therefore recommended to\n"
"          place the '-x'/'--exec' option last.\n"
"          The following placeholders are substituted before the command is executed:\n"
"            '{}':   path (of the current search result)\n"
"            '{/}':  basename\n"
"            '{//}': parent directory\n"
"            '{.}':  path without file extension\n"
"            '{/.}': basename without file extension\n"
"            '{{':   literal '{' (for escaping)\n"
"            '}}':   literal '}' (for escaping)\n"
"          \n"
"          If no placeholder is present, an implicit \"{}\" at the end is assumed.\n"
"          \n"
"          Examples:\n"
"          \n"
"            - find all *.zip files and unzip them:\n"
"          \n"
"                fd -e zip -x unzip\n"
"          \n"
"            - find *.h and *.cpp files and run \"clang-format -i ..\" for each of them:\n"
"          \n"
"                fd -e h -e cpp -x clang-format -i\n"
"          \n"
"            - Convert all *.jpg files to *.png files:\n"
"          \n"
"                fd -e jpg -x convert {} {.}.png\n"
"\n"
"  -X, --exec-batch <cmd>...\n"
"          Execute the given command once, with all search results as arguments.\n"
"          The order of the arguments is non-deterministic, and should not be relied upon.\n"
"          One of the following placeholders is substituted before the command is executed:\n"
"            '{}':   path (of all search results)\n"
"            '{/}':  basename\n"
"            '{//}': parent directory\n"
"            '{.}':  path without file extension\n"
"            '{/.}': basename without file extension\n"
"            '{{':   literal '{' (for escaping)\n"
"            '}}':   literal '}' (for escaping)\n"
"          \n"
"          If no placeholder is present, an implicit \"{}\" at the end is assumed.\n"
"          \n"
"          Examples:\n"
"          \n"
"            - Find all test_*.py files and open them in your favorite editor:\n"
"          \n"
"                fd -g 'test_*.py' -X vim\n"
"          \n"
"            - Find all *.rs files and count the lines with \"wc -l ...\":\n"
"          \n"
"                fd -e rs -X wc -l\n"
"\n"
"      --batch-size <size>\n"
"          Maximum number of arguments to pass to the command given with -X. If the number of\n"
"          results is greater than the given size, the command given with -X is run again with\n"
"          remaining arguments. A batch size of zero means there is no limit (default), but note\n"
"          that batching might still happen due to OS restrictions on the maximum length of command\n"
"          lines.\n"
"          \n"
"          [default: 0]\n"
"\n"
"      --ignore-file <path>\n"
"          Add a custom ignore-file in '.gitignore' format. These files have a low precedence.\n"
"\n"
"  -c, --color <when>\n"
"          Declare when to use color for the pattern match output\n"
"\n"
"          Possible values:\n"
"          - auto:   show colors if the output goes to an interactive console (default)\n"
"          - always: always use colorized output\n"
"          - never:  do not use colorized output\n"
"          \n"
"          [default: auto]\n"
"\n"
"      --hyperlink[=<when>]\n"
"          Add a terminal hyperlink to a file:// url for each path in the output.\n"
"          \n"
"          Auto mode  is used if no argument is given to this option.\n"
"          \n"
"          This doesn't do anything for --exec and --exec-batch.\n"
"\n"
"          Possible values:\n"
"          - auto:   Use hyperlinks only if color is enabled\n"
"          - always: Always use hyperlinks when printing file paths\n"
"          - never:  Never use hyperlinks\n"
"          \n"
"          [default: never]\n"
"\n"
"      --ignore-contain <name>\n"
"          Ignore directories containing the named entry\n"
"\n"
"  -j, --threads <num>\n"
"          Set number of threads to use for searching & executing (default: number of available CPU\n"
"          cores)\n"
"\n"
"      --max-results <count>\n"
"          Limit the number of search results to 'count' and quit immediately.\n"
"\n"
"  -1\n"
"          Limit the search to a single result and quit immediately. This is an alias for\n"
"          '--max-results=1'.\n"
"\n"
"  -q, --quiet\n"
"          When the flag is present, the program does not print anything and will return with an\n"
"          exit code of 0 if there is at least one match. Otherwise, the exit code will be 1.\n"
"          '--has-results' can be used as an alias.\n"
"\n"
"      --show-errors\n"
"          Enable the display of filesystem errors for situations such as insufficient permissions\n"
"          or dead symlinks.\n"
"\n"
"  -C, --base-directory <path>\n"
"          Change the current working directory of fd to the provided path. This means that search\n"
"          results will be shown with respect to the given base path. Note that relative paths\n"
"          which are passed to fd via the positional <path> argument or the '--search-path' option\n"
"          will also be resolved relative to this directory.\n"
"\n"
"      --path-separator <separator>\n"
"          Set the path separator to use when printing file paths. The default is the OS-specific\n"
"          separator ('/' on Unix, '\\' on Windows).\n"
"\n"
"      --search-path <search-path>\n"
"          Provide paths to search as an alternative to the positional <path> argument. Changes the\n"
"          usage to `fd [OPTIONS] --search-path <path> --search-path <path2> [<pattern>]`\n"
"\n"
"      --strip-cwd-prefix[=<when>]\n"
"          By default, relative paths are prefixed with './' when -x/--exec, -X/--exec-batch, or\n"
"          -0/--print0 are given, to reduce the risk of a path starting with '-' being treated as a\n"
"          command line option. Use this flag to change this behavior. If this flag is used without\n"
"          a value, it is equivalent to passing \"always\".\n"
"\n"
"          Possible values:\n"
"          - auto:   Use the default behavior\n"
"          - always: Always strip the ./ at the beginning of paths\n"
"          - never:  Never strip the ./\n"
"\n"
"      --one-file-system\n"
"          By default, fd will traverse the file system tree as far as other options dictate. With\n"
"          this flag, fd ensures that it does not descend into a different file system than the one\n"
"          it started in. Comparable to the -mount or -xdev filters of find(1).\n"
"\n"
"  -h, --help\n"
"          Print help (see a summary with '-h')\n"
"\n"
"  -V, --version\n"
"          Print version\n"
"\n"
"Bugs can be reported on GitHub: https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/issues\n";

MAIN_END
